prompt:
Repo: /home/user/House-building. Read, in this order: docs/CONVENTIONS.md (the law for this repo — golden rule: every number on screen is traceable, prices editable, single offline index.html, phone-first at 390px and fine at 1440px, no external assets), then docs/specs/estimator.md (the approved spec; the owner accepted all three open-question defaults: same room list on every floor, the m² shortcut generates a one-time editable room list, OMR only).

Write the screen spec to /home/user/House-building/docs/specs/estimator-ui.md. English only — ignore your Arabic/RTL habit for this app, the spec puts Arabic out of scope; say so in one line. No existing components exist (empty repo, plain HTML + CSS + vanilla JS), so instead of "components to reuse" define a small set of reusable patterns (card, number input with unit suffix, results table, expandable row) the builder implements once.

The page has two sections, top to bottom:
1. "House material estimator" — inputs (floors, wall height, the m² shortcut, the editable room list with add/remove rows), an editable assumptions & prices panel (collapsed by default; each row: label, value input, unit, source link, last-checked date, a "reset to default" affordance), a Calculate button, and results: a headline row (total blocks, total concrete m³, total steel tonnes, total OMR), then a per-element breakdown table (foundations, columns, beams, slabs, walls × concrete / steel / blocks / wastage % editable / cost). Include empty, error (validation message from the calculator, plain English, never NaN), and "assumptions overridden" states. The builder must expose these hooks for the smoke test: a button with data-action="load-sample" (loads the 2-floor 5-room worked example), a button with data-action="calculate", and the total-blocks headline element with data-result="blocks-total".
2. "How this page was built" — a story section generated from a list of agent dispatch records (fields: order, agent, model, round, prompt, report, outcome, startedAt, finishedAt). Design: a short plain-English intro (1 paragraph) explaining the AI team and one honest note that in a cloud session the main session runs the dev-lead playbook itself, a small org diagram (main session → crew members used), then a vertical timeline, one card per dispatch: step number, agent name, model badge (haiku / sonnet / opus), round badge if round > 1, one-line outcome; each card expands (<details>) to show "What it was asked" (the prompt, monospace, scrollable) and "What it reported back" (the report). Mixed audience: non-technical readers get the story from the collapsed cards, technical readers open the details.

Give: layout at 1440 and 390 (stacking rules), a restrained colour/spacing system defined as CSS custom properties with a dark-mode variant via prefers-color-scheme, typography (system font stack only), and the exact list of DOM ids / data- attributes the builder must use so calc wiring and tests agree. Keep the whole spec under ~250 lines. No code beyond attribute names and CSS variable names.

Your final message: the file path and a ten-line summary of the screens and states.
